steps.text: Sprinkle yeast and 1 teaspoon sugar over ½ cup warm water (about 100 degrees F, 40 degrees C) in a large bowl. Set aside until yeast becomes foamy, about 5 minutes.

Add 3 cups flour, milk, shortening, eggs, ¼ cup sugar, 1 tablespoon oil, and 1 ½ teaspoons salt to yeast mixture; beat with an electric mixer on medium speed until smooth. Add remaining 3 cups flour, ½ cup at a time, mixing well by hand after each addition, until dough comes together; turn out onto a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, about 5 minutes. Dough will be sticky.

Lightly oil a large bowl. Add dough; turn to coat in oil. Cover the bowl with a cloth; set aside to rise in a warm place (80 to 95 degrees F (27 to 35 degrees C)) until doubled in volume, about 1 hour. Punch down dough.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Roll baseball-sized portions dough into "snakes" about 6 inches long; roll each into a spiral to give tops some texture. Set aside.

Combine 4 cups hot water and baking soda in a bowl (baking soda does not need to dissolve completely). Dip each bun in baking soda solution; transfer to a baking sheet. Brush buns with melted butter; sprinkle with coarse sea salt.
Bake in the preheated oven until brown, 20 to 25 minutes. Cool on a wire rack or brown paper bag.

raw_recipe.headline: Pretzel Buns
raw_recipe.description: This pretzel buns recipe tastes and looks like soft pretzels. The buns are great for sandwiches, as a dinner roll, or swap them in place of a burger bun.

review.reviewBody: After reading the reviews, the stickiness of the dough seemed to be an issue, so I reduced the amount of milk to 1-3/4 cups. Kept everything else the same (including 6 cups of A/P flour), and let the KA do all of the kneading. This yielded absolutely beautiful dough so easy to work with. I'm new to yeast bread baking, and I wasn't sure what dipping the dough into the baking soda-water mixture did, but you definitely get a little bit of that taste, and that's a good thing, so don't skip this step. I formed these into different shapes...coiled, square, round, made a few bread sticks, and topped with Trader Joe's kosher salt. Next time I make these, I'll make more bread sticks because they are delicious dipped into mustard. The baked bun texture is perfect, the dough very pliable (not at all sticky), and the flavor similar to the mall pretzels. Thank you for sharing this fabulous recipe...this one is going into my favorites folder.

DOUGH: I made it in the KitchenAid mixer. Many reviews said it was sticky - and I agree. Most reviewers suggest decreasing the milk by 1/4 - 1/2 cup. Instead, I added an extra 1/2 cup of flour and it was perfect!
RISING: My husband was cooking on the barbeque while I was making this, so when the barbeque was turned off, I placed the glass dish of dough on top of the lid, and it rose in about half an hour.
FORMATION: Rolling the dough into snakes and shaping them seemed like a lot of extra effort. I instead just formed balls. In a 9x13 baking dish, I put 8 buns and in a 7x11 baking dish I put 6 - so a total of 14 buns. I cut an X into the top, rubbed the tops with softened butter, and sprinkled with sesame seeds and kosher salt.
FUTURE: It's a very simple recipe and could be adapted to many unique ideas. With a few tweaks, I can easily see this as dinner rolls, hot dog buns, sandwich buns, etc etc. Although I still don't understand the baking soda dip.

Pour yourself some AMAZING pretzel rolls! Yes, the dough is VERY sticky...I'd even say "pourable". But don't let this discourage you. I made the dough in a food processor and used less than 5 cups of flour. After looking at the dough with every flour addition I guessed that it was not going to come together in the "ball". I made and educated guess to stop adding flour and pour in the bowl to rise. It rose beautifully! I dipped the measuring cup in flour and floured my hands too before rolling it out. I heated the water and processed the "buns" like baking bagels...not just a quick dip. These came out perfect...my kids gobbled them up and requested the rolls for their lunchboxes! I am glad I used less flour and mixing because more would have yielded tough rolls. I made larger rolls (that had to be cut in half...they were more like mini-loaves) but next time I will make them smaller (like hamburger/slider size). You can shape the rolls...just take your time and keep your hands/counter floured. Mine were tied in cool knots! This recipe is a keeper! Thank you "Brittsky"!!!...my kids thank you too!

Delicious! Great straight out of he oven. I used a food processor, decreased the milk to 1 3/4 cup as others suggested. I used the rapid rise method so put yeast with 3 cups flour, salt, and sugar. I heated the water and milk, melted the shortening in that and added to the dry mixture. Beat in the eggs and then gradually added the rest of the flour. Kneeled by hand just to form a smooth ball to let rise.

Instead of just dipping in the soda and water solution, boil 4 cups of water in large pot then add soda (it will bubble up) turn down heat so it is simmering. Place the buns one at a time in for 40 seconds maximum. Then put on baking sheet and brush with butter and add salt.

I followed the recipe exactly, except I used instant yeast (and decreased the rise time because of that). I got to the rolling out stage and the six inches note is kinda crazy. Six inches is not nearly thin enough. The first two I only rolled out to six inches and before baking they were the size of my hand. After baking...well I needed one cookie sheet for just those two. The remaining dough I decreased the dough from baseball size per roll to golf ball size roll. The remaining rolls worked out much, much better. They ended up the size of large hamburger buns. If you end up spiraling them make sure you pinch all the ends together as much as you can. I ended up rounding them into flat shapes after dipping because I knew the spirals would come apart in the baking process. The dough recipe itself is fantastic and I will definitely keep it, it’s just the shaping process I didn’t agree with.

These are without a doubt the most tasty pretzel bun I have ever made. We used them for sloppy joes, burgers, sandwiches and just to eat plain. 

The second time I made these I cut the recipe in half and made soft bread sticks for an Italian supper and the family loved them. Brushed them with butter, herbs and parmesan cheese before baking. Freezes well.

A Vegan Alternative - and it's perfect!
I read all the reviews to check for problems and alternatives. I am a vegan, so I used 2 tsp flax seed, ground, with 3 Tbs water for the eggs. I used soy milk for the milk. Also, in my recipe I used 3 tsp yeast, 2 1/2 cups wheat flour, 2 1/2 cups all purpose flour, and oil instead of shortening. 
The dough was not sticky! And the buns came out perfect! They are soft in the inside, and nicely tanned on the outside with a little crunch. I will use this for all my bread recipes in the future.

Excellent recipe. Just for fun, instead of making rolls as described, I pulled of chunks of dough, rolled them flat, added a tiny mound of sausage, cheese and chili sauce, and then gathered up the corners and pinching them to make a stuffed roll. I used ham and cheese for some others. They were excellent and a big hit.

These were amazing! So amazing, that I made them twice in two weeks and they inspired me to try making pretzels again. I followed a user's suggestion to follow the bagel method of 40 seconds in the baking soda solution, and I brushed them with egg wash and sprinkled with poppy seeds before baking (I was out of kosher or pretzel salt). Everyone loved them!
I used the 1-3/4 cup of milk as suggested by another reviewer, I also just put it all in my bread machine using the rapid rise yeast. Perfection!
These get requested again and again.
Great flavor, everyone loves them. Only problem is mine are too flat. Don't know if I over-kneaded them, not enough flour (dough was very sticky), or something else.
Really great! Some tweaks required and I went with an egg wash instead of a butter wash, but really delicious!
I was so intimidated to make this recipe, but it turned out wonderful! I will never again buy store bought pretzel buns! They were perfect for a hot ham and cheese with a spicy honey mustard slider!
These turned out nicely. This is a dense dough and wasn’t exactly what I was looking for but not the recipes fault. These would make FANTASTIC individual soup bowls...clam chowder/chili.
The buns taste amazing, but they did not come out as dark as the pictures suggest even cooking for 25 minutes. Next time I will try for longer.

Typical bun recipe. I wish I'd used a different recipe that didn't have the salt. I used the buns for philly cheesesteak sandwiches and it made them a little too salty and I didn't even use the baking soda. I didn't look at the amount closely and I wasn't about to waste 1/2 cup of baking soda on buns. Instead I brushed the bread with egg before salting it. I only used half of the buns, now I don't know what to do with the rest of them, my family didn't like the salted tops.
Only issue I have is that I end up adding a 7th cup of flour as the dough is too sticky with only 6 cups. Maybe next time I’ll reduce the amount of milk.
